title: feat(spec/ui): export navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource, so a mirror of NavigationItemSchema attaches it by identifier
body:
Fixes #24534

Clause-②: yes (widening)

## What this does

`@objectstack/spec/ui` now exports `navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource`. That is the refinement `NavigationItemSchema` already runs: it refuses a navigation entry with no `dataSource` whose `visible` reads `data`. It is exported the same way as `objectNavTargetExclusivity`, `checkPageRegionPlacement` and `checkPageMainRegionWidth`, so a hand-written mirror of the navigation item can chain the spec's own function instead of restating the rule.

- `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts`: the declaration gains `export`, and its docblock gains the sibling paragraph (what it judges, the issue it raises, who attaches it) After the seat's answer A (comment 6273673166), the function also reads an authored bare-string `visible`. The string goes through `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema`, the slot's own schema, via a module-private `authoredVisibleEnvelope`, so the shorthand normalisation is reused and never restated. The docblock says the function accepts both spellings. The `.superRefine(navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource)` on the union inside `NavigationItemSchema` is unchanged.
- `packages/spec/src/ui/app-nav-visible-data-needs-data-source-export.test.ts`: the export pin (5 legs, 36 tests, below).
- `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`: regenerated by `gen:api-surface` (it reported `touched: ui.json`) and `gen:export-origins` (`1 shard(s) rewritten`). Each gains one row. No other shard moved.
- `.changeset/24534-export-nav-visible-data-check.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. A widening carries no ADR-0087 disposition marker, and `check-adr-0087-registration` is green without one.

Nothing an author can write is accepted or refused differently. The issue is the same: `custom` at `visible`, with the same message. The existing rule pins in `app-nav-visible-data-needs-data-source.test.ts` are untouched and green.

## Premises

**P1 holds.** On `origin/main` `5a871e4e41`:
- `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts:1041` declares `function navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource(item: unknown, ctx: z.RefinementCtx): void` with no `export`.
- `:1107` attaches it with `.superRefine(navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource)` on the discriminated union that `NavigationItemSchema`'s `z.lazy` returns.
- The siblings are `export function checkPageRegionPlacement(` at `page.zod.ts:1766` and `export function checkPageMainRegionWidth(` at `:1846`.

They reach `@objectstack/spec/ui` this way:
- the barrel `src/ui/index.ts` has `export * from './app.zod'` (`:21`) and `export * from './page.zod'` (`:54`);
- `package.json` `exports["./ui"]` maps to `dist/ui/index.{mjs,js,d.mts,d.ts}`;
- each export has one row in `api-surface/ui.json` and one in `export-origins/ui.json`.

So adding `export` is the whole route.

Measured after the build, from `packages/core` (a consumer that resolves the workspace package through its `exports`):
- ESM: `import('@objectstack/spec/ui')` gives `typeof navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource === 'function'`, length 2, resolved to `packages/spec/dist/ui/index.mjs`;
- CJS: `require('@objectstack/spec/ui')` gives `function`, from `dist/ui/index.js`;
- the emitted declaration is `declare function navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource(item: unknown, ctx: z.RefinementCtx): void;`.

**P2 holds for the signature, but not for what a mirror gets when it chains the function as it is.**
- *Signature.* `(item: unknown, ctx: z.RefinementCtx) => void` is what a `superRefine` callback takes. The `ctx` type is the same one `objectNavTargetExclusivity(item, ctx)` takes, and objectui's `NavigationItemSchema` already chains that function. I read objectui `origin/main` `50ba1bb0a6`, `packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts`. That code follows objectui#7715's rule: re-attach the spec's object-level checks by identifier. The function needs no state a mirror would have to supply. Its CEL reader (`celReadsRootData` / `lexCel`) is closed over in the module.
- *Behaviour.* The function judges the entry **after the spec's parse**, where `visible` is the `{ dialect, source }` envelope that `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` produces. Measured on the card's entry, `{ id: 'nav_envs', type: 'object', objectName: 'sys_environment', visible: 'data.total == 1' }`:
  - the door (`NavigationItemSchema.safeParse`) refuses it with one `custom` issue at `visible`;
  - the export called on the same entry with `visible` parsed (`{ dialect: 'cel', source: 'data.total == 1' }`) raises the identical issue: code, path and message;
  - the export called on the entry **as written** (bare-string `visible`) raises **nothing**.
- *objectui's mirror.* It declares `visible: z.union([z.boolean(), z.string()]).optional()`, so its parsed `visible` is still the authored string. Chaining this export there as it is would refuse nothing on the card's entry.
- *What this PR does about it.* The first head (`50c3ba8a4a`) wrote only the export and raised the difference as an open question. The seat answered **A** (comment 6273673166 on this PR): the function also reads the authored bare string, normalised through `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` (the slot's own schema), so the spelling a mirror hands it is judged exactly as the spec's parse would judge it. Measured on `e058ce508e`:
  - the card's entry as written now draws the door's identical issue (code, path and message) from a direct call;
  - the same bare string with a `dataSource` draws nothing;
  - a boolean or absent `visible` judges nothing.

  `NavigationItemSchema` accepts and refuses exactly what it did, because its own check only ever sees the parsed envelope. The schema pins in `app-nav-visible-data-needs-data-source.test.ts` are unchanged and green (23 passed).

## The pin (`app-nav-visible-data-needs-data-source-export.test.ts`, 36 tests)

1. **Parity.** Over 8 fixtures (4 refusing branches: `object`, `dashboard`, `url`, `group`; 4 accepting paths: the card's entry with a `dataSource`, an ambient-root predicate, a member named `data`, and no `visible`), the direct call and `NavigationItemSchema.safeParse` agree issue for issue. These fixtures write `visible` as the envelope, the one spelling whose parsed value equals what was written.
2. **Mount.** The union the lazy schema resolves to carries exactly one `custom` check, and its issue vector over the matrix equals the export's.
3. **Attachment by identifier.** The source declares `export function navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource(` once and chains `.superRefine(navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource)` once, on a code line.
4. **Barrel identity.** `./index` exports the same function object, with arity 2.
5. **Both spellings.**
   - The card's bare-string entry is refused by the door.
   - The export raises the door's identical issue on the entry's parsed `visible` and on the entry as written.
   - Over the leg-1 matrix rewritten with bare strings (7 rows: 4 refusing, 3 accepting), the direct call and the door agree issue for issue.
   - The control (the same bare string with a `dataSource`) draws nothing from the door or the export.
   - A boolean or absent `visible` judges nothing.

**Ablation (reverse verification), at `42945c2f43` with the implementation committed.** The mutation was `export function navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource(` → `/* ablated: export removed */ function navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource(`, applied through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`:
- landed on disk: anchor 1 → 0, blob `8755bfe0b8eb` → `07a6fe68bd65`;
- result: **22 failed / 5 passed (27)**, red as predicted;
- restored: blob == HEAD `8755bfe0b8eb`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

The test imports `./app.zod` and `./index` relatively (src, not `dist`), so the ablation needed no rebuild. The first attempt was a no-op: the replacement text was a substring of the anchor, and the tool refused before it ran anything. It was re-run with a distinct marker. (That reading is at the first head, where the pin had 27 tests.)

**Ablation of the bare-string read, at `e058ce508e` with the patch committed.** The mutation was `const visible = (typeof entry.visible === 'string'` → `const visible = (/* ablated: bare-string read removed */ false && typeof entry.visible === 'string'`, through `ablation-replace.mjs`:
- landed on disk: anchor 1 → 0, blob `74d3de955a29` → `c459f2d5767d`;
- result, running this file with `app-nav-visible-data-needs-data-source.test.ts`: **5 failed / 54 passed (59)**;
- exactly the new legs went red: the as-written leg and the 4 refusing rows of the bare-string matrix;
- the accepting rows, the controls and the whole schema pin file stayed green;
- restored: blob == HEAD `74d3de955a29`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Tests and gates (final head `e058ce508e`)

`origin/main` `c3954057fe` was merged at `50c3ba8a4a` through `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`. Main's later commits touch no file this PR touches, so it was not merged again.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: 702 files passed, 21348 tests passed, 1 todo.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`, `check:scripts-typecheck` and `check:test-typecheck` all pass. The test-typecheck debt is unchanged at 52 files / 242 errors / 132 pinned signatures, so the new test adds no errors.
- The new pin file alone: 36 passed. The schema pin `app-nav-visible-data-needs-data-source.test.ts` is unchanged since `50c3ba8a4a` and passes 23.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: `All 14 generated artifacts are up to date`, against the `dist` this head built. `check:api-surface` reports `public API surface + factory signatures unchanged`, and `check:export-origins` reports `current`.
- The derived gate list (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, no paths, 89 commands, identical before and after the merge) was run on this head with each exit code captured before any pipe. **All 89 exited 0.** `dispatch-gates --ran` answers: `89 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 89 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 89 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)`. This includes `check:api-surface`, `check:export-origins`, `check:entry-nameability`, `check:browser-reachable-entries`, `check:dual-source-exports`, `check:exported-any`, `check:docs`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check:published-files`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:type-check-debt`. On both heads, three of them (`check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`) first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, nothing measured) in a freshly created worktree. They exited 0 once their packages were built, and `--ran` records those exit-0 re-runs.
- Local-only: `check:dev-prereqs` exit 0 and `check:skill-frame-freshness` exit 0.
- CI check-runs on `e058ce508e` (40 runs), read when the patch report was written: every required context except `Test Core (6/6)` is green (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core (1/6)` to `(5/6)`). `Test Core (6/6)` then went red on a runtime share-link case that timed out at vitest's 5000 ms default. That failure is not this PR's (seat CI note 6274396318) and is filed as #24633. Its one re-run is in flight. The patch report on #24534 cites the check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- **The open question, answered A by the seat (comment 6273673166).** The function now reads an authored bare-string `visible` as well as the parsed envelope, so objectui's mirror can attach the export as it is, by identifier. B (objectui restates the shorthand) and C (objectui takes `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` by reference) are not taken here. C stays objectui's own call for its boolean and envelope divergences.
- **Read-only observation, not filed.** objectui's `visible` arm differs from the spec's in two more ways. It accepts `visible: true` / `false`, which the spec's `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` refuses. It refuses the `{ dialect, source }` envelope, which the spec accepts. I read this from the source and did not measure it through `objectui validate`. It belongs to the objectui follow-up this card names (Done-when 2).
